files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.GrammarKind
files.Summary: Provenance label of an IGrammar (ABI v7).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.IChunkWallClock
files.Summary:
Wall-clock seam for per-chunk prefill timing (INF BL-33).
    The native prompt commit is synchronous, so the wall measured around it IS
    the chunk wall on whatever backend is compiled in (metal / cuda / vulkan /
    cpu — backend-independent by construction); the seam exists so tests can
    script timings instead of sleeping.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.ILoraAdapter
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 9): a loaded LoRA adapter (opaque native handle).
Loaded against ONE model (arch-matched, typed on mismatch); attached to
contexts via IInferenceContext.SetAdapters. Weights-surface modifier:
KV-neutral, attach/detach mid-conversation without rewind.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.IPrefillStallDetector
files.Summary:
Typed stall detector over per-chunk prefill wall timings
    (INF BL-33). Stateful across the chunks of one prefill: it maintains the
    rolling baseline itself.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.ISpeculationSuspender
files.Summary:
Runtime suspension of the speculative helper (draft/ngram) on the
    owning executor stack — the real native wiring for the stall-safe prefill
    ladder's DraftDisabledRetry rung (INF BL-33b). Implementations must be
    idempotent (suspending with no active session is a no-op, mirroring the
    native pvx_executor_spec_free contract) and must not throw when the
    helper is already disabled.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.IStallRecoveryLadder
files.Summary: Facade view of the stall-recovery ladder (INF BL-33): owns the configured step order and the retry budget; returns the step for a given 0-based retry attempt and fails closed when the budget is exhausted (the caller is expected to throw the typed unrecovered error then — the ladder itself never invents steps). Surfaced behind the Engines facade (StallWatchdogOps.CreateRecoveryLadder) so callers never touch the Implementation namespace.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Abstractions.ITtsSession
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 7): a TTS session — a SEPARATE decode context on
the backbone speech model plus a gen-audio mmproj. Never entangled with a
conversation context (KV-neutral by construction). Capability-truthful:
creation against a mmproj without a gen-audio pipeline throws typed.
Determinism: identical (text, request.Seed) pairs replay byte-identically.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Abstractions.IDecisionHeaderReader
files.Summary:
Decision-model file validation seam (load state machine step). A REAL
protobuf scan of the ONNX ModelProto wire (ir_version, graph IO signature
names, opset_import presence) — long initializers are skipped by seek, so a
500MB+ model validates in milliseconds. Any structural violation throws —
the load state machine maps that to fail-closed model_invalid before any
session init is attempted.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Abstractions.IDecisionSessionFactory
files.Summary:
Creates <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSession" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>s for a decision (judge) model file:
builds the ORT session options (full graph optimization, matching the
training runtime) and walks the parsed <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ExecutionProviderChain" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
in preference order. EP FALLBACK RULE: a provider that fails to initialize
degrades to the next entry — CPU is always the terminal fallback and is the
only provider REQUIRED to work. The session's ACTUALLY-active provider is
recorded so health reporting is truthful. One factory per host; thread-safe.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Abstractions.IExecutionProviderDefaultSource
files.Summary:
Per-OS DEFAULT execution-provider chain for decision models: applied when a
model configures NO explicit execution_provider. Injected so tests can pin
the OS.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionAssetCatalog
files.Summary:
Resolves the judge ASSET files (tokenizer.json, judge-spec-*.json) for one
configured judge model. Resolution order (first hit wins):
  1. model config "file" SIBLING directory (a bundled model dir ships both),
  2. the server root's assets/models/judge/ directory,
  3. next to the server binary (Assets/models/judge copied at build/pack time).
Spec file per record kind: judge-spec-shell.json / judge-spec-process.json.
Pure resolver — performs no IO beyond existence checks at Resolve time.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionHeaderReader
files.Summary:
Wave-2 ONNX header validation: a REAL protobuf scan of the ModelProto wire —
ir_version (field 1, varint), the graph message (field 7) with its input
(field 11) and output (field 12) ValueInfoProto names, and opset_import
presence (field 8). Long initializers are SKIPPED by seek (never read into
memory), so a 500MB+ model validates in milliseconds. Any structural
violation throws — the load state machine maps that to fail-closed
model_invalid before any session init is attempted.
Wire-format reference: developers.onnxruntime.ai/onnx/proto (ModelProto,
GraphProto, ValueInfoProto field tables). Pure scanner — no state.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionRecord
files.Summary:
One judged decision record, validated and normalized (parser → executor boundary).
SHELL records carry command+cwd; PROCESS records carry the os/exe/chain/cmd/net/writes
tuple. The untrusted SHELL "purpose" field deliberately has NO field here — it is
echoed in audit logs only and never reaches decision input.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSession
files.Summary:
ONE loaded ONNX judge model ready for batch inference: the ORT session
(selected execution provider recorded), the tokenizer, the sequence spec,
and the row collation + decode that mirrors the training evaluation exactly.
Disposal releases the session. NOT thread-safe per instance beyond the
session's own safety — the executor serializes inference per engine.

Decode (training-eval semantics, per question row k = option count):
  choice  → argmax over the k class logits → JudgeAction (allow/sandbox/deny);
  noul    → softmax over 2, P(true) = NeedsSandbox;
  score   → softmax over 5, expected value = Risk (0..4);
  confidence → max class probability after temperature scaling (0..1).
The Jev raw wire (JudgeQuestionSet) decodes ARBITRARY caller questions instead:
choice → argmax option label + per-option probabilities, score → expected level
value + level-index probabilities, noul → P(true) — same softmax/temperature
machinery, no escalation.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSessionFactory
files.Summary:
Creates <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSession" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>s for a judge model file: builds the ORT
session options (full graph optimization, matching the training runtime) and
walks the parsed <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ExecutionProviderChain" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> in preference order
(LLM-10 per-OS chains). EP FALLBACK RULE: a provider that fails to initialize
(not bundled, driver/library problems, unsupported ops) degrades to the next
entry — CPU is always the terminal fallback and is the only provider REQUIRED
to work. The session's ACTUALLY-active provider is read back from the runtime
(a silent ORT fallback to CPU counts as a fallback, not as GPU) and recorded
so /pvx/health `active_execution_provider` is truthful. One factory per host;
thread-safe (stateless beyond the injected option applier).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionTestSupport
files.Summary:
Test-support surface for the decision engine slice (Inference-side, consumed
by both repos' test suites): opens an ORT session with ONE pinned provider.
Keeping the only direct ORT-construction site inside ProvostXInference is the
LLM→Inference extraction contract — LLM-side code references no ORT types.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.EpAttempt
files.Summary:
One candidate configuration for an EP session init: a label for
    diagnostics and the options mutation it applies. Ordered — first that
    successfully creates a session wins.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ExecutionProviderChain
files.Summary:
Parsed execution-provider chain for a decision (judge) model (e.g. "cpu",
"coreml->cpu", "cuda->cpu"). First entry is the preferred provider; later
entries are fallbacks. Unknown names fail config validation loudly (the
parser throws) — silent CPU fallback for typos is a misconfiguration hazard.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ExecutionProviderOptionsApplier
files.Summary:
Per-EP session-option presets (LLM-10): each configured chain entry may need
provider-specific session options (CUDA device id, DirectML device id, ROCm
device id, OpenVINO device type, CoreML flags). Every preset list ends with a
PLAIN name-append fallback so a quirk mismatch never fails an otherwise
loadable provider — remaining failures fall down the chain to cpu (never fail
when cpu works). Instance type, no state — cheap to construct, injectable.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeAction
files.Summary: Judge verdict actions. The FINAL action in the wire response is produced by JudgeVerdictMapper, which owns the risk-escalation rule — the executor's raw action may be upgraded (allow → require_approval) but never downgraded.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeModelNotReadyException
files.Summary:
Typed fail-closed judge error: every judge endpoint maps this to HTTP 503 with
a machine-readable code — NEVER to a 200/allow verdict. Codes:
"model_unloaded" (judge engine present but not loaded) and "model_missing"
(no judge model configured/registered for the requested id).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeNumericsGate
files.Summary:
Canonical numerics gate (LLM-10): before a NON-CPU execution provider is
accepted, the judge model must reproduce the canonical wave-4 anchor (the
destructive `dd` deny — recorded on the CPU EP: deny EXACT, conf ≈ 0.9231,
risk ≈ 3.128) within tolerance. A GPU/CoreML EP that loads but drifts the
anchors is REJECTED and the chain continues to the next provider (cpu always
terminates). Fail-closed: gate evaluation errors count as drift.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeOption
files.Summary:
One rendered option of a judge question: its answer label and its
criterion description (null = no description — rendered as the bare label).
Option ORDER is decision-meaningful (argmax index → label). Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeQuestionAnswer
files.Summary:
ONE raw model answer for one Jev question (session decode → response mapper
boundary). RAW semantics: the model's argmax choice / expected score / noul
probability — NO risk-escalation rule applied (the escalation owner is
JudgeVerdictMapper on the enriched arms; the raw wire stays raw).
Field populations per type: choice → Choice + Confidence + Probabilities;
score → Score + Confidence + Probabilities (level-index keyed) + Legend;
noul → Noul. Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeQuestionAnswerSet
files.Summary:
The raw answers for ONE Jev request (one state), in question order, plus the
USAGE inputs: the tokenized state length (actual tokenizer count of the
serialized state — the usage.input_tokens definition) and the question count
(the usage.output_tokens definition: one answer per question). Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeQuestionDef
files.Summary:
One typed judge question as trained (id, type, instructions, ordered options).
Pure data — the judge spec carries these in the exact training order
(action, needs_sandbox, risk_level).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeQuestionRowSet
files.Summary:
Encoded question rows for ONE Jev state + the pre-truncation token count of
the serialized state (usage.input_tokens source). One row per question, in
question order. Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeQuestionType
files.Summary:
Judge question types, numbered EXACTLY as the judge models were trained
(laya QTYPES): choice=0, score=1, noul=2. The value feeds the model's
qtype input — never renumber.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeRecordKind
ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeRowEncoding
files.Summary:
Encoded ONE question row of a judge record: token ids, marker (MASK) offsets,
and the question's type. One record → one row per question, in question order.
Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeScore
files.Summary:
Raw model output for one judged record (executor → response mapper boundary).
The mapper owns the risk-escalation rule; the executor reports raw scores only.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeSequenceEncoder
files.Summary:
Builds judge model input rows from validated <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionRecord" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>s:
serializes the record EXACTLY as the training pipeline did (compact JSON with
the mask token stripped), then assembles
[CLS] {type} question: {instructions} [SEP] [MASK] opt0 [MASK] opt1 ... [SEP] {state} [SEP]
per question, with the state tail capped to the sequence budget. Mirrors the
training sequence builder (head budget 256, options capped at 48 tokens each)
against the committed fixtures (Tests/Assets/judge/seq-fixtures.json).
One encoder per judge model spec; thread-safe (stateless + immutable fields).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeSequenceSpec
files.Summary:
The FULL serialized inference specification for one judge model: record kind,
sequence budget (max_len/head_max_len exactly as trained), the confidence
temperatures fitted at export time, and the three typed questions in training
order. Loaded from a spec JSON (Assets/models/judge/judge-spec-*.json) —
the questions MUST match the training questions verbatim or the model scores
text it was never trained on.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeStateQuestions
files.Summary:
One decision-engine question batch on the Jev wire: the SERIALIZED state text
(rule owned by the server layer's state serializer — the engine plane only sees
text) and the typed questions to answer. Questions = null → the judge's
CANONICAL trained question set (the loaded session's spec — our additive
default for omitted questions; real Jev requires questions). One request → one
answer set. Pure data.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.JudgeTokenizer
files.Summary:
Deterministic BPE tokenizer for the Laya judge models (mmBERT vocabulary,
HuggingFace tokenizer.json format: BPE model + Replace(" " → "▁") normalizer
+ Metaspace pre-tokenizer, add_special_tokens=False semantics — no BOS/EOS
post-processing; the judge sequence builder places CLS/SEP itself).

Pipeline (replicates the training tokenizer byte-for-byte):
  1. added-token extraction (longest match, pre-normalization, per segment),
  2. normalization: " " → "▁" per non-added segment,
  3. Metaspace pre-tokenization: prepend "▁" when the segment does not start
     with it, then split BEFORE every "▁" (each "▁" begins a piece),
  4. greedy lowest-rank BPE merges per piece (pairs of in-vocab symbols only),
  5. unknown symbols: byte fallback ("<0xXX>" tokens), then <unk>
     (consecutive unknowns fused).

Thread-safe: all mutable state is ConcurrentDictionary caches; encoding is a
pure function of the input text. Deterministic: no RNG, no time, no IO after
construction. Verified against the training pipeline on the committed vector
fixture (Tests/Assets/judge/tok-vectors.json).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.OnnxExecutionProvider
files.Summary:
Execution providers for decision (judge) models. The chain is parsed and
validated at config time so unknown names fail loudly. Per-OS: CoreML
(macOS), DirectML (Windows), CUDA/ROCm/OpenVINO (Linux) — cpu is always the
terminal fallback.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.OsExecutionProviderDefaultSource
files.Summary:
Per-OS default EP chains (LLM-10): macOS coreml→cpu, Windows directml→cpu,
Linux cuda→rocm→openvino→cpu — first available wins at session init; cpu is
always the terminal fallback. An injected osOverride keeps the mapping
testable without touching the real host OS.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.DecisionEngineOps
files.Summary:
Decision lane ops over an existing <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSession" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (loaded by
the factory through <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Abstractions.IDecisionSessionFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.DecisionEngineRequest
files.Summary:
Contract for an ONNX decision (judge) engine on the managed ORT lane:
model path, tokenizer JSON, judge sequence-spec JSON, execution-provider
chain (raw string, LLM-10 format; null = OS default), optional numerics gate.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.DecisionEngineRequestBuilder
files.Summary:
Fluent builder for <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.DecisionEngineRequest" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (ONNX judge lane).
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.DecisionEngineRequestBuilder.Build" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> yields a VALIDATED request (fail-closed).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EncoderEngineOps
files.Summary: Encoder lane ops: wraps the vision encoder + backing model (see interface).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EncoderEngineRequest
files.Summary:
Contract for a vision ENCODER engine: a GGUF model (for its vocabulary/
tokenizer context) plus a REQUIRED mmproj projector. The engine's primary
lane is image embedding; generative GGUF ops are NOT exposed on this kind.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EncoderEngineRequestBuilder
files.Summary:
Fluent builder for <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.EncoderEngineRequest" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (vision encoder lane:
GGUF model + REQUIRED mmproj). <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.EncoderEngineRequestBuilder.Build" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> yields a VALIDATED request.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineKind
files.Summary:
Which backend lane an <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> serves. One engine object
per lane; the facade routes ops views by this kind (fail-closed on mismatch).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineLogging
files.Summary:
Facade view of the native logging bridge (owner black-box directive
2026-10-19): native C-level log setup is a process-wide facade concern
(the pvx_set_log_* entry points dispatch on the ACTIVE engine's tables),
so callers configure it here instead of reaching into the Logging
namespace. Pure delegation — identical semantics, facade-only surface.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineMaintenance
files.Summary:
Facade view of the offline engine-maintenance utilities (owner black-box
directive 2026-10-19): file-level operations that need NO loaded engine
object but ARE engine-bound (they dispatch on the ACTIVE engine's
per-handle tables). Currently: GGUF tokenizer-metadata repair (EOG/special
token fixup — weights stream-copied byte-for-byte, metadata rewritten).
Pure delegation to the Implementation layer — callers never leave the
facade surface.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineRequest
files.Summary:
The typed engine CONTRACT base: everything a caller must tell Inference to get
an <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. Derived records add lane-specific parameters.
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineRequest.Validate" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> is fail-closed — any invalid field throws
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Exceptions.InvalidEngineRequestException" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> before a backend is ever touched.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineOps
files.Summary:
GGUF lane ops implementation over the wrapper-layer graph. Holds the model,
the live context (created from the request's context settings), and the pool
(lazily created on first <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineOps.LeaseConversation" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>). Disposal flows
outward-in via the owning <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngine" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineRequest
files.Summary:
Contract for a GGUF generative engine on the native llama.cpp backend:
model path, optional vision projector (mmproj) sidecar, optional speculative
draft-model sidecar, and the full native load knob set (BL-02 engine matrix,
GPU layers, threads, flash attention, KV type, reasoning markers) plus
context sizing. Knobs are load-time; live knobs live on the engine object.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineRequestBuilder
files.Summary:
Fluent builder for <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineRequest" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineRequestBuilder.Build" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> yields a
VALIDATED request (fail-closed); <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufEngineRequestBuilder.Create(ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngineFactory)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> builds + factory-creates
an engine in one step.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufModelLoader
files.Summary:
Production <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IGgufModelLoader" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: thin wrapper over the native
wrapper-layer factories (<xref href="ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceModel.Load(ProvostXInference.Models.ModelConfig)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> +
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Abstractions.IInferenceModel.LoadVisionEncoder(System.String)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>). No state, no fallback.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IDecisionEngineOps
files.Summary:
Decision (ONNX judge) lane ops view: batch judging on the ORT session with
truthful active-provider reporting, plus the tokenizer/spec the caller needs
to build records. Wraps <xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.DecisionSession" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; adds nothing native.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IEncoderEngineOps
files.Summary:
Encoder lane ops view: image embedding through the mmproj projector mounted
on the GGUF model's context. Text embeddings are reachable via the Gguf-style
model context; this view keeps the vision lane honest and minimal.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IGgufEngineOps
files.Summary:
GGUF lane ops view: the full native llama.cpp surface as properties/methods —
context management, KV-cache operations, sampling knobs, speculative knobs.
Wraps the existing wrapper-layer graph (model → context → pool → conversation);
the raw abstractions stay reachable for advanced callers.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IGgufModelLoader
files.Summary:
Testability seam over the native GGUF loader: the engine factory depends on
THIS interface, not on <xref href="ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceModel" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>'s static
factory, so the facade is unit-testable without a native image.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine
files.Summary:
The SOLE caller-facing object of Inference's world: one loaded backend (GGUF
llama.cpp, ONNX decision, or vision encoder) behind a typed facade with
lifecycle, inference ops, context management, KV-cache ops, and every knob
as a property. Callers (e.g. ProvostXLLM) hold an array of these and route
requests by <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine.Kind" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>/<xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine.ModelPath" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngineFactory
files.Summary:
Resolves a validated <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.EngineRequest" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> into an UNLOADED
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.IInferenceEngine" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. Constructor-injected backend seams keep this
unit-testable without native images.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngine
files.Summary:
Facade implementation: created UNLOADED by <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngineFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>,
loaded on <xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngine.Initialize" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> per kind, torn down on Dispose (ops first,
then backend). All deps constructor-injected; no static state.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngineBuilder
files.Summary:
Fluent entry point of the engine-object contract: 
var engine = InferenceEngineBuilder.Gguf("/path/model.gguf")
    .WithMmproj("/path/mmproj.gguf").WithGpuLayers(99)
    .Build();                    // → validated GgufEngineRequest
engine.Create(factory).Initialize();   // → live IInferenceEngine
No static mutable state — the builder is a local, disposable scratch record.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.InferenceEngineFactory
files.Summary:
Default factory (composition root of the facade): native GGUF loading via
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Engines.GgufModelLoader" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (thin seam over the wrapper-layer static
factory), decision loading via the existing
<xref href="ProvostXInference.Decision.Abstractions.IDecisionSessionFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> lane. No static mutable state.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Engines.StallWatchdogOps
files.Summary:
Facade factory for the stall-watchdog helper family (INF BL-33, owner
black-box directive 2026-10-19): the rolling-median detector, the
recovery ladder and the production wall clock are ENGINE-LEVEL utilities
(backend-independent, pure managed) — but callers must consume them
through the facade surface, never the Implementation namespace. This
static factory is the sole construction seam; the returned types are the
Abstractions interfaces. Fail-closed: a null/invalid config throws (the
underlying helpers validate in their constructors).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Exceptions.EngineKindMismatchException
files.Summary: Fail-closed typed error for accessing an ops view of the wrong kind (e.g. engine.Decision on a Gguf engine). The facade never hands out a null view — it refuses.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Exceptions.InferenceException
files.Summary:
Thrown when a native ProvostXInference call returns an error code.
    Base of the typed-error family (engine contract, LDC audit 2026-10-17).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Exceptions.InvalidEngineRequestException
files.Summary:
Fail-closed typed error for an invalid engine contract (bad/missing path,
out-of-range knob, wrong-kind field). Thrown BEFORE any backend is touched.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Exceptions.PrefillStallUnrecoveredException
files.Summary:
Fail-loud terminal outcome of the stall-safe prefill recovery
    ladder (INF BL-33): a prefill chunk kept stalling past the configured
    retries. Carries the evidence (chunk index, wall, baseline, steps
    attempted) so the failure is diagnosable — never a silent hang or a
    quiet degradation.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.ChunkedStallSafePrefillRunner
files.Summary:
Engine-level stall-safe chunked prefill layer (INF BL-33).
     Independent of downstream orchestration AND backend-independent by
     construction: it leases conversations from the injected pool, commits the
     prompt in chunks via PromptTokens, and times each chunk commit with pure
     wall-clock around the synchronous native prompt call — the pvxinference
     substrate dispatches to whatever backend is compiled in (metal / cuda /
     vulkan / cpu), and this layer never knows or cares which. No backend
     timing hook exists or is required; wall-clock is the sole detection
     mechanism, so detection behaves identically on every backend. On stall it
     walks the configured recovery ladder (fresh-slot retry → smaller-chunk
     retry → draft/ngram disabled → fail loud).

     Honesty notes:
     - A fresh-slot retry re-prefills the committed prefix on the new slot (the
       new slot starts with an empty KV), so it is correct, not cheap.
     - The draft/ngram-disabled step suspends the speculative session through a
       constructor-injected <xref href="ProvostXInference.Abstractions.ISpeculationSuspender" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (real native
       wiring: pvx_executor_spec_free via ExecutorSpeculationSuspender). When
       no suspender is wired, that step fails closed with the typed unrecovered
       error naming the missing seam — never a silent skip.
     - With <xref href="ProvostXInference.Models.StallWatchdogConfig.Enabled" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> = false the runner performs
       a single plain prompt commit (watchdog fully inert).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.ExecutorSpeculationSuspender
files.Summary:
Runtime draft/ngram suspension backed by the executor's native
    speculative-session teardown (pvx_executor_spec_free; INF BL-33b).
    Idempotent by construction — the native teardown is already idempotent and
    the suspension is recorded so a second Suspend is a managed no-op.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.GgufMetadataRepair
files.Summary:
GGUF tokenizer-metadata repair (owner 2026-10-06): some HuggingFace GGUFs omit
the EOS token from tokenizer.ggml.special_eog_ids — the engine's native EOS
stop then never fires and generation runs past end-of-turn. The native
pvx_repair_eog_metadata rewrites the METADATA ONLY (weights stream-copied
byte-for-byte); this is the public managed facade over it. Dispatches on
the ACTIVE engine's per-handle dispatch tables (BL-02).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeControlVector
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 10): wraps a pvx_cvec_t (control-vector direction
file). Loaded via NativeInferenceModel.CreateControlVector (n_embd-matched,
typed refusal naming both dims on mismatch); all dispatch goes through the
OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables. Applied to contexts via
NativeInferenceContext.SetControlVector; weights-surface modifier
(KV-neutral, live attach/detach).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversation
files.Summary:
Wraps a leased pvx_conversation_t. Does NOT own the handle — the pool does.
Dispose() returns it to the pool if not already returned. All calls dispatch
on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (carried from the pool at lease).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversationPool
files.Summary:
Wraps a native pvx_pool_t. All calls dispatch on the OWNING
    ENGINE's per-handle tables (flowed from the context's model); a leased
    conversation carries the same tables for its own calls.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversationSpecSession
files.Summary:
Speculative session bound to ONE pooled conversation (ABI v7,
    feature 5): enable/generate/stats over pvx_conversation_spec_*, with the
    active-config mirror kept honest by routing every mutation through
    Enable/Disable below (same discipline as the executor lane). The native
    pool-return/teardown paths free the session natively; <xref href="ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversationSpecSession.OnReturned" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
    clears the managed mirror so it can never report a phantom session.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversationState
files.Summary:
Wraps a conversation state (pvx_conversation_save). Token count
    queries dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables
    (constructor-injected, carried from the conversation at save time).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeGrammar
files.Summary:
Wraps a pvx_grammar_t. Created through — and dispatching on — the
    OWNING MODEL ENGINE's per-handle tables.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceBackend
files.Summary:
Backend safety layer (pvx_probe_backend + queries). The probe is
    context-anchored and dispatches on the OWNING CONTEXT ENGINE's per-handle
    tables; the process-wide queries dispatch on the ACTIVE engine — a no-op
    passthrough until a model load activates it.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceContext
files.Summary:
Wraps a native pvx_context_t. All calls dispatch on the OWNING
    MODEL ENGINE's per-handle tables (injected via the model).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceModel
files.Summary:
Wraps a native pvx_model_t. Factory: Load(). BL-02: EVERY pvx_* call this
model (and everything created from it) makes is dispatched through the
OWNING ENGINE's per-handle dispatch tables — resolved once at engine open
and injected down the whole object graph; no global P/Invoke routing.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeInferenceState
files.Summary:
Wraps a pvx_state_t (pvx_state_save). Token count queries dispatch
    on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (constructor-injected).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeLoraAdapter
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 9): wraps a pvx_adapter_t (LoRA). Loaded via
NativeInferenceModel.CreateLoraAdapter (arch-matched, typed on mismatch);
all dispatch goes through the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables. Attached
to contexts via NativeInferenceContext.SetAdapters; adapters are freed on
Dispose (and by the model at its teardown — native contract).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeStandardExecutor
files.Summary:
Wraps a pvx_executor_t (standard, non-batched path). All calls
    dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (flowed from the context).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeTtsSession
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 7): wraps a pvx_tts_session_t — a SEPARATE decode
context on the backbone speech model plus a gen-audio mmproj (never a
conversation context; KV-neutral by construction). All calls dispatch on
the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeVisionEncoder
files.Summary:
Wraps an mmproj context for vision/image encoding. All calls
    dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (constructor-injected).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.PvxDefaultEngineSelector
files.Summary:
Platform default engine selection — used when the model config leaves the
engine field unset: macOS resolves to the metal specialist; Windows/Linux
prefer cuda when its specialist file ships, else vulkan, else the cpu
engine (every platform can build a CPU specialist); fail-closed
(typed error, no silent fallback) when none is installed. The OS identity
is constructor-injected (same probe family the selector matrix consults —
no hidden environment dependence). Stateless utility — no mutable state.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.RollingPrefillStallDetector
files.Summary:
Rolling-median stall detector (INF BL-33). A chunk is a stall when
    its wall exceeds GapMultiplier × the rolling median of the recent baseline
    window. The detector is silent (never a stall) until the baseline holds at
    least MinBaselineSamples clean observations — the first chunks of a prefill
    cannot be judged against an empty baseline.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.StallRecoveryLadder
files.Summary:
Recovery ladder for the stall-safe prefill layer (INF BL-33).
    Owns the configured step order and the retry budget; returns the step for
    a given 0-based retry attempt and fails closed when the budget is
    exhausted (the caller is expected to throw the typed unrecovered error
    then — the ladder itself never invents steps).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Implementation.SystemChunkWallClock
files.Summary:
Production wall clock backed by the injected <xref href="System.TimeProvider" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
    (constructor injection, no statics — INF BL-33).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Interop.PvxLogDelegate
files.Summary:
Log callback delegate (pvx_set_log_callback). Must be rooted by the caller
for the process lifetime — the native side stores the raw function pointer.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Logging.IInferenceLogger
files.Summary:
Minimal logging seam for Inference-side subsystems (decision judge execution,
build-on-first-use helpers). The host application injects an adapter over its
own logger; the default sink drops everything (non-fatal diagnostics only).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Logging.NativeLogBridge
files.Summary:
Bridges native C-level logging (pvx_set_log_callback) to a managed callback.
Encapsulated in the Inference layer — no dependency on LLM or Core loggers.
The caller provides an Action<int,string,string> that forwards to whatever
logger they have (LLM's ServerLogger, Core's Logger, console, etc.).
Per-handle dispatch (BL-02): the pvx_set_log_* entry points are invoked on
the ENGINE'S OWN dispatch tables (resolved via the active per-handle
dispatch route) — never the global static route — so logging state lives in
the specialist module that owns the model. The delegate thunk itself must
still be pinned for the process lifetime (the native side stores the raw
function pointer).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Logging.QuietInferenceLogger
files.Summary:
Silent logger fallback (diagnostics are non-fatal — when no logger is
    injected they are dropped rather than crashing the caller).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.AudioChunk
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 6): one raw PCM audio clip for prompt-with-audio.
Mono F32 samples at the projector's NATIVE sample rate (probe via
IInferenceModel.AudioSampleRate; product code never resamples — a rate
mismatch is the caller's typed failure). One clip per record.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.BackendInfo
files.Summary: Snapshot of backend probe results.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.ContextConfig
files.Summary: User-facing context configuration.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.EngineStats
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 12): copy-out stats snapshot of one lane
(executor or conversation). Spec counters mirror the spec telemetry
(0/0 when no session is active); rejected drafts derive as drafted-accepted.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.EngineTelemetry
files.Summary:
ABI v9 (per-engine telemetry, owner order 2026-10-22): MODEL-aggregate
snapshot — the roll-up of every executor/conversation lane on ONE engine
instance (never process-wide). Rates (tok/s etc.) are derived by the
caller between two snapshots; the engine stays stateless. Counters never
hide failures: rejected spec drafts derive as Drafted - Accepted.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.KvOverrideTag
files.Summary: Tag for a GGUF metadata override value (BL-21b wave-5).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.KvType
files.Summary: Managed enum mirroring PvxKvType.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.ModelConfig
files.Summary: User-facing model configuration (not blittable — converted to PvxModelParams internally).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.NgramConfig
files.Summary:
n-gram speculative-dcoding knobs (ABI v6). Active iff the
    speculative mode is an n-gram mode; zero values select the per-mode native
    defaults. Sentinel discipline mirrors the rest of SpeculativeConfig:
    the config is blitted to pvx_ngram_params_t at the native boundary.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PoolingType
files.Summary: Managed enum mirroring PvxPoolingType.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PrefillRecoveryStep
files.Summary:
Recovery-ladder step executed after a detected prefill stall
    (stall-safe prefill layer, INF BL-33). Ordered from cheapest to
    fail-loud; the ladder always terminates in <xref href="ProvostXInference.Models.PrefillRecoveryStep.FailLoud" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
    so a persistently stalling prefill never spins silently.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PrefillStallVerdict
files.Summary:
Typed result of one stall-detector observation (INF BL-33).
    Immutable; carries the evidence so callers can log or fail with real
    numbers instead of a bare boolean.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PvxEngineSelectionError
files.Summary:
Typed failure of engine-selection validation
    (fail-closed contract — every invalid pair or unknown id resolves to one of
    these, never to a guessed default).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PvxEngineSelector
files.Summary:
Validates the ModelConfig engine field against the 5-product engine matrix:
result object over (engine id, OS probe) — unknown ids and wrong-OS
selections fail closed with a typed error; no default engine guessing here.
Stateless utility — no mutable state.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PvxEngineSpec
files.Summary:
A selected per-model engine: a validated (engine, OS) specialization from
the 5-product matrix — the file-name contract lives exclusively in the
Interop policy/resolver layer (names in ONE place). The ModelConfig engine
field selects WHICH specialist dylib runs for this model; the resolver
rejects unknown engines and wrong-OS selections fail-closed.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.PvxEngineValidation
files.Summary:
Outcome of engine-selection validation: exactly one of a validated
    spec or a typed fail-closed error (never both, never a guessed default).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.SamplingConfig
files.Summary: User-facing sampling configuration.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.SpeculationStats
files.Summary:
Spec-session acceptance telemetry for ONE speculative session
    (executor or pooled conversation; ABI v7 adds the conversation lane):
    cumulative drafted/accepted token counters since session start. Zero/zero
    when no session is active — counters never hide rejections.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.SpeculativeCapabilities
files.Summary:
The engine's self-reported speculative capabilities for ONE loaded
    model: a supported-types list (SpeculativeType bitset), not booleans.
    A report of None means the model supports no native speculative type — the
    second draft model (SpeculativeMode.Draft with a user-provided draft model)
    remains the available option whenever DraftSimple is reported.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.SpeculativeMode
files.Summary:
Speculative-decoding mode, values mirror pvx_spec_mode_t exactly.
    Fail-closed rule: a configured path that cannot be honored (missing/unloadable
    draft model, missing capability, wrong vocab family) is a typed error naming
    the boundary — never a silent fallback to non-spec generation.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.SpeculativeType
files.Summary:
Supported speculative-decoding types, mirrored from the llama.cpp
    speculative enum via the engine's self-report (PVX_SPEC_TYPE_* bits).
    The ENGINE decides what the loaded MODEL supports — query
    IInferenceModel.SpeculativeCapabilities per model load and offer exactly
    these types for sequential mode; never assume.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.StallWatchdogConfig
files.Summary:
Configuration for the engine-level stall-safe prefill watchdog
    (stall_watchdog config section; INF BL-33). Defaults follow the owner
    decision: multiplier 5 over the rolling median chunk wall, 3 retries, the
    full four-step recovery ladder.

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.TtsRequest
files.Summary:
ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 7): TTS knobs. Zero values select the per-model
upstream defaults (native mtmd_gen_inp_default); Seed == uint.MaxValue
selects a random draw (fixed seeds replay byte-identically).

files.Title: ProvostXInference.Models.TtsResult
files.Summary: TTS generation result: raw PCM F32 mono at the pipeline rate.
